text.p: Following are some of the top headlines in leading Italian newspapers.

* Prime minister Romano Prodi drew criticism from both politicians and prosecutors after defending Giulio Andreotti, seven times premier and now on trial for alleged links to the Mafia. In an interview published on Sunday in a German newspaper, Prodi said he could not believe Andreotti, a leading Christian Democrat, protected the mob during his long carrier (all). In an interview, Andreotti said he was grateful to Prodi for believing in his innocence (La Repubblica).

* Italian ideas to bring forward the start of European economic and monetary union met the opposition of German Chancellor Helmut Kohl and Finance minister Theo Waigel after Italian Prime Minister Prodi expressed conecern that political paralysis in Germany might harm the planned launch of EMU (all).

* Petrol prices are expected to fall about 10 to 20 lire per litre starting from today following the slight rise of the Italian lira against the U.S. dollar. Agip and IP should be the first companies to apply price reductions, followed by the rest (all).
** Reuters has not verified these stories and cannot vouch for their accuracy.
